summary.intent: Win the Lio 'Keep the Line Running' hackathon challenge for Soony by analyzing the supplier/ERP data drops, finding hidden launch risks, and building a generic recheck-and-act agent product (poller, versioned store, extraction, reconcile, approve-and-send actions, dashboard).
summary.outcome: Found that Collector's Edition would miss launch (overbooked art books, failed statues, stale packing counts), produced briefing docs/pages and interview questions, and built and committed a working app with watcher, paper check, site questions, reconciled shipment status, editable email review and UI fixes (274 tests passing). A drop rehearsal and several supplier/teammate follow-ups remain in progress.

repo: Portal API has only list files, get file, and archive.zip endpoints; no webhooks, so change detection means polling the file list and comparing SHA-256 (files can be replaced under the same name).
Confidential portal data lives in gitignored data/; .env is gitignored and .env.example is committed with an empty token.
Entire only writes a checkpoint when repo files change; a session with no modified files logs 'skipping checkpoint', which is not a hook failure.
Team workflow files CLAUDE.md and PROGRESS.md exist; tasks are claimed with a Now line in PROGRESS.md and multiple builders edit api.py concurrently, so commits must wait until builders report.
Outbound email is guarded by an allow-list of known supplier addresses (cardtools.supplier_addresses()/known_addresses()); the server refuses unknown To/CC even if the UI is bypassed.

Teammate Lucas's branch origin/new-approach (pulse-console/server.mjs) sends emails via the shared mailbox without the allow-list; it sent confusing mails to Hwaseong and one to an external Gmail address with order data.

The hand-kept Excel tracker was read only by the verifier; the app used only soony/erp/open_shipments.csv, which is frozen since Fri 20 Nov 17:00. Tracking.py now reconciles all sources with precedence: goods receipt, site answer, supplier doc/reply, tracker, export, other sheets.

Several drops are not fully used: JSON supplier profiles (Pune 'watch', PackRight 'at risk') only had emails read, CPO memo .docx is unreadable by the recognizer, launch_status.xlsx is unused, and the news case is lost because two modules write the same file.
Karton Nowak's 50,000-sleeve rush offer contradicts its own downtime notice (15,000 max) and nothing flags it.
The Collector's lid-magnet shortage is a false alarm: PackRight fits the magnets into the box.

code.finding: A later `_MONEY` regex overrides an earlier one with the same name; the new cost regex was renamed to avoid the clash. Routing/status decisions must run after final status ('half done') is known, not before.
Generic site-question model (packed/received/count) with staleness thresholds via ASK_* env vars; answers stored in data/state/floor_counts.json.
Reconciles shipment status across all sources; floor.receipts() treats any receipt on the same order/part as booked regardless of date, which could hide a site question (TODO left).

Source links inside claim sentences must be inline spans with button behaviour, since <button> blocks cause stray line wraps; the chosen option is now clickable with a numbered key matching options 2-4.

workflow: Delegate large builds to background subagents but avoid committing shared files until all builders report, to prevent committing half-finished work.
Check for teammates' edits and Docs-doc edits before overwriting, and run tests, ruff, tsc and a build before each commit.
Send outbound mail only after approval, only to known addresses, and avoid guessing salutations; use profile names (saved as a memory rule).
Don't send multiple emails to the same supplier within minutes; Lio warns that spammed suppliers may stop cooperating.
